title: Pills/ToggleButtonGroup: all options render with "selected" style on fresh page load in Safari
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

On fresh page load (before any user interaction), st.pills (multi-select mode) renders ALL options with the "selected" purple-outline style in Safari, even though no option is selected — the underlying server-side state (default=None) is correctly empty. The visual bug appears specifically in real Safari and does not reproduce in Chromium or Playwright's WebKit engine.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

selected = st.pills(
    "Filter",
    options=["Option A", "Option B", "Option C"],
    selection_mode="multi",
    default=None,
)
st.write(selected)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open the app fresh in Safari (macOS or iOS) — a new tab/window, not a warm reload.
2. Before clicking anything, observe the st.pills widget with selection_mode="multi" and default=None.
3. All options render with the "selected" purple-outline styling, even though nothing has been selected yet.
4. The underlying state is correct (st.write(selected) shows an empty list) — this is a visual-only bug.
5. Does NOT reproduce in Chromium or in Playwright's WebKit engine — only in real Safari.

### Expected Behavior

On fresh load with default=None, all pill options should render in the plain/unselected style, matching the actual empty selection state.

### Current Behavior

All pill options render in the "selected" style (purple outline/fill) on fresh page load in Safari, despite no option being selected and the server-side value correctly being an empty list.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0
- Python version: (from your requirements.txt / Railway build — Claude Code can confirm the exact version)
- Browser: Safari (macOS) — reproduces on real Safari; does not reproduce in Chromium or Playwright's WebKit
- OS: macOS

### Additional Information

Extracted the relevant CSS from the live page's compiled stylesheet:
[data-selected]:not([data-disabled]) { background-color: rgba(79,70,229,0.1); border-color: rgb(79,70,229); color: rgb(79,70,229); }

This appears to be an attribute-presence selector issue: in Chromium/WebKit-via-Playwright, react-aria (the underlying ToggleButtonGroup implementation) correctly omits the data-selected attribute entirely on unselected buttons, so the selector doesn't match. It's possible real Safari's DOM/CSS engine handles react-aria's attribute timing differently on initial paint, causing data-selected to be briefly (or persistently) present on all buttons before Safari's own attribute-removal logic runs — worth investigating from the react-aria/Safari interaction side.

Visual-only Safari bug: on a cold load, multi-select `st.pills` with `default=None` paints every option with the primary selected style even though widget state is correctly empty. This is plausible in code: after the BaseWeb → React Aria migration, `StyledPillsToggleButton` (and the shared `st.segmented_control` styles) key off the presence selector `[data-selected]:not([data-disabled])`. CSS `[data-selected]` matches any present attribute, including `data-selected="false"` or `""`, so a Safari/react-aria first-paint quirk that leaves that attribute on unselected `ToggleButton`s would produce exactly this screenshot while Chromium and Playwright WebKit (not real Safari) stay clean. The hosted repro not reproducing is consistent with that. Worth checking `st.segmented_control` in real Safari the same way, and inspecting whether unselected buttons have `data-selected` / `data-selected="false"` in the DOM.

### Related Issues

- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12802 — Same `ToggleButtonGroup` CSS surface (`[data-selected]` / hover adjacency) for `st.segmented_control`; not a duplicate, but the closest existing styling bug on this component.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12912 — Selected *appearance* of `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control` diverging from the actual value (disabled case). Same class of visual/state mismatch, different trigger.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12388 — Earlier report that pills hide the selected style when `disabled=True`; inverse of this issue (selected look missing vs. selected look on everything), same widget.

No duplicate of the Safari cold-load “all pills look selected” report was found.

---
*This is an automated triage comment using `cursor-grok-4.6-xhigh`. Please verify the suggested labels and related issues.*
This would be a genuinely useful fix/addition for the project.

Thanks for the detailed report — the CSS you extracted was genuinely useful in narrowing this down. I spent some time trying to reproduce it in real Safari and wasn't able to, so I want to share exactly what I tried in case it helps us find the difference between our setups.

**What I tested:** Streamlit 1.64.0 (your reported version) in a clean venv, your snippet verbatim, with `primaryColor = "#4F46E5"` set so the selected style matches the indigo in your CSS. Real Safari 26.6.2 on macOS 26.7 — not Playwright's WebKit, since your report rules that out. Three loads: a first-ever visit to the URL, a warm reload, and one on a separate origin so every asset was refetched cold. On all three, the three `default=None` pills rendered plain: no `data-selected` attribute, `aria-pressed="false"`, and a neutral `rgba(49,51,63,0.2)` border rather than the indigo one.

**Why I trust that negative result:** a "nothing found" outcome is only as good as the detector, so the same page also had a second pills widget with `default=["Ctrl A"]` as a control. That button reported `data-selected` present with `background-color: rgba(79,70,229,0.1); border-color: rgb(79,70,229); color: rgb(79,70,229)` — exactly the CSS you quoted. So the check does see the attribute and the indigo styling when they're really there; the `default=None` pills simply didn't have either. I also sampled every animation frame from before React first rendered through several seconds after, specifically to catch a transient flash on first paint, and there were zero frames where an unselected pill carried the attribute.

**On the attribute-timing theory:** I don't think this one can be it, unfortunately. In the shipped bundle react-aria emits the attribute as `data-selected={isSelected || undefined}`, and React removes rather than sets an attribute whose value is `undefined`. So `data-selected=""` or `data-selected="false"` never exists on an unselected button in any engine — there's no attribute present for `[data-selected]` to match, and no window for Safari to remove it late. Related: the compiled rule on the page is class-scoped (`.st-emotion-cache-XXXX[data-selected]:not([data-disabled])`) rather than the bare `[data-selected]` selector, though that's secondary to the attribute never being there.

Since you're clearly seeing it, I suspect something in your app that the minimal snippet doesn't have. Two things would help a lot:

- Your exact Safari version, and whether it was macOS or iOS. I could only test 26.6.2 on macOS, and I don't have an iOS device to check.
- Whether the app has any custom CSS, a theme beyond `primaryColor`, or custom components. This follows on from the question above — anything injecting styles that match `.stButtonGroup button` could paint the pills without any `data-selected` involved.

If you can still reproduce it, running this in Safari's console on the affected page would tell us which half of the problem it is:

```js
document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid=stButtonGroup] button').forEach(b =>
  console.log(b.textContent.trim(), '| data-selected:', b.hasAttribute('data-selected'), '| border:', getComputedStyle(b).borderColor))
```

If `data-selected` comes back `true` on options you haven't clicked, it's a state bug and I'd want your Safari version to chase it. If it's `false` but the border is still indigo, then something other than that rule is doing the painting, and whatever custom CSS is in the app is the place to look.
Closing as team unable to repro
